newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed - gasoil down with futures.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed - gasoil down with futures.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Thursday, traders said.
Gas oil outright values fell across the board with front month July IPE closing $3 lower at $164.50 a tonne.
Physical trade was very quiet. Traders saw demand into Greece and Italian islands for four cargoes of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil loading in the latter part of next week.

But they said the demand was not urgent because delivery dates were flexible and as a result buyers were not yet showing numbers. Russian heating oil remains assessed at a very notional cif high quotes +$2.50/$3 basis Genoa.
Gasoline remains supported by Nigerian demand and dealers said the Mediterranean was set to strengthen against NWE although outright prices may be pressured lower by falling crude.
Eurograde cargoes were steady at $186.00 fob Med.
Naphtha was slow, but prices held. "In the short-term its steady, but I think there will be lower numbers over the next few days," said one dealer. Fob cargoes were put at $166.
High sulphur was steady but the market seemed a little tight with no avails seen expect for a few cargoes held by an Italian refiner, some 40,000 tonnes or more.
Little Russian supplies of cracked material were seen on the market, but traders said an M-40 straight run was sold on Wednesday by a Spanish refiner loading out of Odessa.
The seller and a second Spanish refiner were heard looking around the market for some cracked cargoes.
Traders said they were awaiting results of a tender for the supply of 30,000 tonnes of 4 percent sulphur fuel oil to Dakkar.
Activity was also thin on the one percent front, after a 50,000-tonne cargo on offer by a Spanish refiner was said to have been withdrawn from the market.
